Journal.Title: Pediatrics international : official journal of the Japan Pediatric Society

Article.ArticleTitle: Prognostic Markers in Congenital Diaphragmatic Hernia: Left Ventricular Diameter and Pulmonary Hypertension.

Abstract.AbstractText: The aim of the study is to predict prognosis of newborns with congenital diaphragmatic hernia (CDH) with the left ventricular diameter and estimated pulmonary artery pressure values.

Patients in the newborn unit in 2012-2016 were screened retrospectively. Echocardiographic measurements of 35 patients with isolated left lateral CDH and 25 healthy newborn were compared in the first 24h of life.

The mean values ​​of left ventricular end-diastolic (LVEDD) and end-systolic (LVESD) diameters, and ejection fraction were significantly lower in the patients. Moreover, tricuspid insufficiency (TR) and pulmonary insufficiency (PR) were significantly higher than controls (p<0.001). Six patients died within the next 40 days after birth. Mean values ​​of LVEDD and LVESD were significantly lower in patients who died when compared to discharged (p<0.001, p=0.016). Also, mean ​​values of TR and PR (p<0.001) and the frequency of pulmonary hypertension (PPH) (p=0.001) were significantly higher in these patients. In the ROC analysis of the patients who died LVEDD<11 mm [sensitivity 100% (95% CI:87.9-100) and specificity 100% (95% CI:54.1-100) and TR>3.5m/s [sensitivity 89.66% (95% CI:72.6-97.7) and specificity 100% (95% CI:54.1-100)] were demonstrated to be associated with poor prognosis.

In this study, decrease in LV diameter and presence of pulmonary hypertension was shown to be associated with poor prognosis. Also, presence of PPH was found to be associated with mortality in patients with CDH. Thus, it is assumed that, in the follow-up prognosis may be predicted by a carefully echocardiographic evaluation of the LV diameters and pulmonary pressures. This article is protected by copyright.
